description_full: Poste Italiane S.p.A. provides postal, logistics, and financial and insurance products and services in Italy. The company operates through four segments: Mail, Parcels and Distribution; PostePay Services; Financial Services; and Insurance Services. Its Mail, Parcels and Distribution segment engages in the mail, parcel, and logistics activities, as well as provision of welfare services. The PostePay Services segment provides payment management and e-money services through a network of LIS sales points, as well as mobile and fixed telephone services and electricity and gas sales services. Its Financial Services segment engages in the placement and distribution of financial and insurance products and services, such as current accounts, postal savings products, mutual funds, financing, insurance policies, and activities. The Insurance Services segment is involved in the investment, retirement, and protection businesses through the issuance of life and P&C insurance products. The company was founded in 1862 and is based in Rome, Italy.

financial_summary: POSTE ITALIANE SPA is a large-cap industrials business with a $42.9B market cap on $25.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +11% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Gross margins of 27% are the starting point for assessing pricing power.

The business throws off $1.7B in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.22× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 54× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 3.9% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 52% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
